title: Coordinated Experiment Orchestration — Greenroom Notes
content:
Purpose
- Capture ad-hoc decisions and small protocols for cross-functional rollouts before we formalize into the rollout playbook. This is the "greenroom" — quick, low-friction runbook drafts, role notes, and experiment choreography we test in the next two quarters.

Audience
- Product leads, Eng on-call, SRE, Observability, Solutions Eng, CS for post-release monitoring.

High-level goal
- Make small-slice experiments safe and repeatable across teams with minimal ceremony. Let product teams drive iterations while engineering and SRE surface guardrails and fast fallbacks.

Key principles (short)
- Minimum friction: enable 5–20% slices in <1 hour of ops prep for low-risk changes.
- Observable gates: every activation must have 3 primary signals + at least 2 secondary signals instrumented.
- Defined fallback choreography: who flips the switch, how traffic is rebalanced, and how customers are notified.
- Cost and latency awareness: experiments carry explicit budget and latency windows.

Greenroom vocabulary (incubation terms we use here)
- Incubation slice: initial small traffic cohort (0.1–5%) for experimental behavior.
- Conductor: person who owns activation and immediate triage (usually product PM).
- Backstage: SRE/infra/observability on-call pairing during first 2 hours of activation.
- Cueboard: ephemeral dashboard that aggregates the 3 primary signals for the experiment.

Preflight checklist (fast, can be run in Slack thread)
- Owner assigned (Conductor): name, slack handle.
- Objective + success metric: single sentence + expected effect size.
- Activation recipe: percent slices, cohorts, target regions.
- Primary signals (choose 3): e.g., error rate (p99 error count), latency (p95 tail), user-visible failure rate.
- Secondary signals (optional, >=2): cost/tokens per request, model quality regression metric from eval harness, API credit churn.
- Rollback plan: immediate percent cut (e.g., cut to 0% or reroute to baseline model), who authorizes, communication plan.
- Cost guardrail: $/hour or token budget for first 24 hours.
- Observability hooks live: cueboard URL, traces, alert thresholds created.

Activation choreography (quick recipe)
1) T-minus 30m: Conductor posts final activation note in experiment thread + pings Backstage. Confirm cueboard link and alerts.
2) T-minus 10m: dry-run traffic plan in staging traffic-sim tool (if available) or run smoke tests.
3) Activate to Incubation slice (0.1–1%)
4) Observe for 10–30 minutes (fast watch window): check primary signals at 1, 3, 10 minutes.
5) If stable, increment to target small slice (up to 5%) in steps (1%, 2.5%, 5%) with 10–30m holds.
6) If any primary signal trips threshold, follow rollback plan immediately and post postmortem note in thread.

Signal matrix (example for a model change experiment)
- Primary 1: p95 latency (region/global) — threshold: +40% above baseline or >600ms absolute (whichever stricter).
- Primary 2: user-visible failure rate — threshold: >0.5% absolute increase vs baseline or >3x current.
- Primary 3: model hallucination token score on sampled prompts (daily mini-eval) — threshold: >10% regression.
- Secondary A: token cost per request — threshold: budget consumption > 30% of daily allotment in first 6 hours.
- Secondary B: tail memory pressure on serving nodes — threshold: OOM events >0 in 12 hours.

Roles and responsibilities (fast mapping)
- Conductor (product): owns objective, activation, stakeholder comms.
- Eng lead (feature): owns rollout configuration, quick-engineering fix if needed.
- Backstage lead (SRE): watches infra signals, ready to cut traffic or scale.
- Observability owner: ensures cueboard + alert fidelity.
- CS/Support rep: watches customer tickets and triages with priority.

Fast rollback templates (copy-paste for incident thread)
- Title: [Rollback] <experiment-name> — immediate action taken
- Time: <ISO time>
- Action: Rolled experiment back to baseline model; cut percent 7 -> 0.
- Reason: Primary signal <name> breached threshold (attach logs/links).
- Next steps: assign owner for investigation; schedule 1-hour postmortem.

Experiment variants and A/B bookkeeping
- Keep variant tags simple: V0 (baseline), V1 (candidate), V1a (candidate+latency-optim), V1b (candidate+token-pricing).
- Store mapping in experiment-config repo + a single source of truth spreadsheet (link back to linked_artifacts).
- When doing A/B, prefer even splits only after passing incubation. Early traffic must be skewed toward baseline.

Mini-eval harness (lightweight)
- Run a daily sample of 200 canned prompts through both baseline and candidate. Compute 3 quick metrics: relevance score, hallucination flag rate, length distribution. Fail fast if hallucination increases > 8pp.
- Integrate eval output into cueboard for human-on-call to glance at.

Conflict and escalation paths (short)
- If Conductor and Backstage disagree on rollback: Backstage has temporary veto for safety-critical infra signals. Product resumes authority after immediate mitigation and a 15-minute sync.
- Legal/Security blocks: if flagged, Backstage will cut experiment to 0% until security sign-off.

Lightweight postmortem template (to use after any rollback or unexpected degradation)
- TL;DR (2 sentences)
- Timeline (key timestamps)
- What happened (short)
- Root cause hypothesis
- Immediate mitigations taken
- Long-term actions and owners
- Customer impact + comms

Open questions / TODOs
- Can we add a tiny traffic-sim plugin to Console that simulates the slice behavior with current request distribution? (priority: medium)
- Decide standard incubation slice increments and hold times by risk category. Proposed: low risk (0.5% -> 2% -> 5%, 10m holds), medium (0.1% -> 1% -> 3%, 30m holds), high (manual gating).
- Hook mini-eval and cost metrics into the A/B experiment API so we get automatic failure signals.

Notes from last trial (2025-08 rapid run)
- We rolled model V1 to 1% incubation across EU-West only. Cueboard showed p95 spike for 3m then returned to baseline; spike correlated with a small batch of long-sequence requests.
- Action taken: Backstage increased pooling and cache TTL, re-routed >1k long-sequence requests to dedicated pool. No rollback.
- Learnings: add a preflight short-scan for sample sequence-length distribution before activation.

Small checklist for engineers implementing activation hooks
- Expose experiment-tag in request headers so logs can be filtered easily.
- Emit sample-id for trace correlation for 1 in N requests (default N=100).
- Metric names: use standardized prefix experiment.<name>.(latency|errors|tokens|quality).
- Provide a minimal API that flips a variant at route-level and returns current allocation percentages.

Communication primitives (short)
- Experiment thread template (Slack): header, Conductor, objective, activation plan, cueboard link, rollback template.
- Customer comms: one-sentence notification if experiment affects SLA or known behavior.

Appendix: quick links and snippets
- Minimal curl to flip variant (internal):
  curl -X POST 
    -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' 
    -H 'Content-Type: application/json' 
    https://console.internal.redwood/api/experiments/activate 
    -d '{"experiment":"<name>", "variant":"V1", "percent":1}'

- Quick SQL to sample request distribution (internal analytics):
  SELECT region, percentile_cont(0.95) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY request_time_ms) AS p95_ms, count(*) 
  FROM requests WHERE created_at > now() - interval '24 hours' GROUP BY region ORDER BY count DESC LIMIT 25;

If you're reading this and want to try a small experiment tomorrow: pick a Conductor, fill the preflight checklist, ping Backstage and post the cueboard link. We'll iterate this doc into a formal playbook in Q1.'
